items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: some of the other orchestras such as Lloyd Scott, Alfonso Trent, Horace Henderson and Speed Webb

ctx.x: But the band was just as great as it had been the first time I heard it and the Armory was crowded. We of the Helvey orchestra left Cincy for Lexington full of praise for Fletcher Henderson and his orchestra and we felt as though we had gotten religion and were on our way to heaven instead of Lexington.

An orchestra came to Cincinnati in 1926 from New York under the direction of a man named Alex Jackson. It was mostly a society orchestra of 10 musicians: 2 trumpets, trombone, 3 saxes and 4 in the rhythm section. With the leader Alex who sometimes played soprano sax, they were 11. This orchestra had nothing in common with Fletcher Henderson or some of the other orchestras such as Lloyd Scott, Alfonso Trent, Horace Henderson and Speed Webb because they did not play the kind of jazz music that I had heard from…

They made a big hit with the women, and wherever the women went, the men were sure to be there. So Alex stayed in the vicinity of Cincinnati for months and even worked at a white open air dancing place on Vine Street in Walnut Hills where no other negro orchestra had ever worked. Walnut Hills is a suburb of Cincinnati.
